evidence.quote: For the electrospray fabricated PSCs . The glass/ITO substrate was cleaned by ultrapure water and ethanol for 35 min and then blown dry with a a nitrogen gun and treated with ultraviolet-O3 for 30 min. For the NIP device structure, the SnO2 electron transport layer (2.5%, diluted by water) was deposited on the ITO by spin-coating at 4000 rpm for 25 s, then annealed at 150 ℃ for 30 min in air. Before perovskite fabricating, the ITO/ SnO2 needs to UV-ozone treated for 15 min. Then put the substrate on the plat acceptor of the electrospray machine which was 60 mm below the nozzle, set the voltage to 20 KV and push speed to 0.001 mm/min.

For the electrospray fabricated PSCs . The glass/ITO substrate was cleaned by ultrapure water and ethanol for 35 min and then blown dry with a a nitrogen gun and treated with ultraviolet-O3 for 30 min. For the NIP device structure, the SnO2 electron transport layer (2.5%, diluted by water) was deposited on the ITO by spin-coating at 4000 rpm for 25 s, then annealed at 150 ℃ for 30 min in air. Before perovskite fabricating, the ITO/ SnO2 needs to UV-ozone treated for 15 min. Then put the substrate on the plat acceptor of the electrospray machine which was 60 mm below the nozzle, set the voltage to 20 KV and push speed to 0.001 mm/min.

The operational stability of PSC devices was first evaluated by tracking the photovoltaic performance evolution under the open-circuit condition. ES-based p-i-n PSCs (with the device architecture of ITO/PTAA/Perovskite/C 60 /BCP/Au) retained 86% of their initial PCE (17.87% ± 0.48%) after 1056 h of illumination (white LED lamp, 100 mW cm -2 ). In contrast, SP-based devices only kept 65% of their original PCE (17.51% ± 0.87%) under the same conditions (Figure 3c). The PL spectra of corresponding devices are shown in Figure 3e,f, and a significant red shift ( ≈ 38 nm) was observed in SP samples alongside the broadened FWHM (from 53 to 89 nm in Table S6, Supporting Information) (Figure 3e).

For the PIN device structure, the PTAA (2 mg/mL in CB) HTL was spin-coated on the ITO substrate at 4000 rpm for 25 s, then annealed at 120 ℃ for 3 min. Before perovskite film depositing, a pure DMF was spin-coated at 5000 rpm for 25 s. The perovskite film fabricated by electrospray is consistent with the above description. After perovskite film depositing, GACl (2 mg/mL in IPA)/OAmI (0.4 mg/mL in IPA) mixing solution were spin-coated on the perovskite film at 5000 rpm for 25 s and annealed at 100 ℃ for 5 min. Then the C60 (25 nm) and BCP (6 nm) were thermally evaporated at rate of 0.2 and 0.1 Å s -1 on to the perovskite films sequentially.

For the PIN device structure, the PTAA (2 mg/mL in CB) HTL was spin-coated on the ITO substrate at 4000 rpm for 25 s, then annealed at 120 ℃ for 3 min. Before perovskite film depositing, a pure DMF was spin-coated at 5000 rpm for 25 s. The perovskite film fabricated by electrospray is consistent with the above description. After perovskite film depositing, GACl (2 mg/mL in IPA)/OAmI (0.4 mg/mL in IPA) mixing solution were spin-coated on the perovskite film at 5000 rpm for 25 s and annealed at 100 ℃ for 5 min. Then the C60 (25 nm) and BCP (6 nm) were thermally evaporated at rate of 0.2 and 0.1 Å s -1 on to the perovskite films sequentially.

ES-based p-i-n PSCs (with the device architecture of ITO/PTAA/Perovskite/C 60 /BCP/Au) retained 86% of their initial PCE (17.87% ± 0.48%) after 1056 h of illumination (white LED lamp, 100 mW cm -2 ). In contrast, SP-based devices only kept 65% of their original PCE (17.51% ± 0.87%) under the same conditions (Figure 3c). The PL spectra of corresponding devices are shown in Figure 3e,f, and a significant red shift ( ≈ 38 nm) was observed in SP samples alongside the broadened FWHM (from 53 to 89 nm in Table S6, Supporting Information) (Figure 3e).
The device was finished by thermal evaporation of Au or Cu (100 nm) under vacuum.

processing_steps.operation: spin-coat PTAA HTL and anneal

evidence.quote: For the PIN device structure, the PTAA (2 mg/mL in CB) HTL was spin-coated on the ITO substrate at 4000 rpm for 25 s, then annealed at 120 ℃ for 3 min. Before perovskite film depositing, a pure DMF was spin-coated at 5000 rpm for 25 s. The perovskite film fabricated by electrospray is consistent with the above description. After perovskite film depositing, GACl (2 mg/mL in IPA)/OAmI (0.4 mg/mL in IPA) mixing solution were spin-coated on the perovskite film at 5000 rpm for 25 s and annealed at 100 ℃ for 5 min. Then the C60 (25 nm) and BCP (6 nm) were thermally evaporated at rate of 0.2 and 0.1 Å s -1 on to the perovskite films sequentially.

processing_steps.operation: alternative ES perovskite deposition and annealing

evidence.quote: The perovskite solution was deposited on the substrates through electrospray system and the deposited perovskite films were transformed hot-plate and annealed at 120 ℃ for 20 min. All electrospray coating and annealing processes were carried out in ambient conditions. After that, the OAI solution (0.024 M, dissolved in isopropanol) was spin-coated with 5000 rpm for 30 s to form a passivation layer. Then the Spiro-OMeTAD (75 mg mL -1 ) + PTAA (10 mg mL -1 ) / CB with the addition of hole transport layer 35 μL Li-TFSI / acetonitrile (260 mg mL -1 ), and 30 μL 4-tertbutylpyridine, was deposited by spin-coating at 3500 rpm for 30 s.

For the electrospray fabricated PSCs . The glass/ITO substrate was cleaned by ultrapure water and ethanol for 35 min and then blown dry with a a nitrogen gun and treated with ultraviolet-O3 for 30 min. For the NIP device structure, the SnO2 electron transport layer (2.5%, diluted by water) was deposited on the ITO by spin-coating at 4000 rpm for 25 s, then annealed at 150 ℃ for 30 min in air. Before perovskite fabricating, the ITO/ SnO2 needs to UV-ozone treated for 15 min. Then put the substrate on the plat acceptor of the electrospray machine which was 60 mm below the nozzle, set the voltage to 20 KV and push speed to 0.001 mm/min.

The operational stability of PSC devices was first evaluated by tracking the photovoltaic performance evolution under the open-circuit condition. ES-based p-i-n PSCs (with the device architecture of ITO/PTAA/Perovskite/C 60 /BCP/Au) retained 86% of their initial PCE (17.87% ± 0.48%) after 1056 h of illumination (white LED lamp, 100 mW cm -2 ). In contrast, SP-based devices only kept 65% of their original PCE (17.51% ± 0.87%) under the same conditions (Figure 3c). The PL spectra of corresponding devices are shown in Figure 3e,f, and a significant red shift ( ≈ 38 nm) was observed in SP samples alongside the broadened FWHM (from 53 to 89 nm in Table S6, Supporting Information) (Figure 3e).

processing_steps.operation: electrospray perovskite deposition and annealing

evidence.quote: For the electrospray fabricated PSCs . The glass/ITO substrate was cleaned by ultrapure water and ethanol for 35 min and then blown dry with a a nitrogen gun and treated with ultraviolet-O3 for 30 min. For the NIP device structure, the SnO2 electron transport layer (2.5%, diluted by water) was deposited on the ITO by spin-coating at 4000 rpm for 25 s, then annealed at 150 ℃ for 30 min in air. Before perovskite fabricating, the ITO/ SnO2 needs to UV-ozone treated for 15 min. Then put the substrate on the plat acceptor of the electrospray machine which was 60 mm below the nozzle, set the voltage to 20 KV and push speed to 0.001 mm/min.

processing_steps.operation: spin-coat GACl/OAmI mixing solution and anneal

evidence.quote: For the PIN device structure, the PTAA (2 mg/mL in CB) HTL was spin-coated on the ITO substrate at 4000 rpm for 25 s, then annealed at 120 ℃ for 3 min. Before perovskite film depositing, a pure DMF was spin-coated at 5000 rpm for 25 s. The perovskite film fabricated by electrospray is consistent with the above description. After perovskite film depositing, GACl (2 mg/mL in IPA)/OAmI (0.4 mg/mL in IPA) mixing solution were spin-coated on the perovskite film at 5000 rpm for 25 s and annealed at 100 ℃ for 5 min. Then the C60 (25 nm) and BCP (6 nm) were thermally evaporated at rate of 0.2 and 0.1 Å s -1 on to the perovskite films sequentially.

Then the Spiro-OMeTAD (75 mg mL -1 ) + PTAA (10 mg mL -1 ) / CB with the addition of hole transport layer 35 μL Li-TFSI / acetonitrile (260 mg mL -1 ), and 30 μL 4-tertbutylpyridine, was deposited by spin-coating at 3500 rpm for 30 s.

In addition, we performed the SPO tracking of unencapsulated devices under one-sun irradiation (white LED lamp, 100 mW cm -2 ) in N 2 . Based on the p-i-n device architecture, after 1550 h, the ES-based device still preserved 90% of its initial PCE, while the SP-based device only kept 53% under the same condition (Figure 3d). For the n-i-p architecture (ITO/SnO 2 /perovskite/Spiro-OMeTAD + PTAA/Au), the ES-based PSC could still maintain 74.7% of its initial PCE after 568 h of aging, whereas only 32.7% of the original PCE was retained in the SP-based device (Figure S22, Supporting Information).
The device was finished by thermal evaporation of Au or Cu (100 nm) under vacuum.

processing_steps.operation: clean glass/ITO substrate and UV-O3 treat

evidence.quote: For the electrospray fabricated PSCs . The glass/ITO substrate was cleaned by ultrapure water and ethanol for 35 min and then blown dry with a a nitrogen gun and treated with ultraviolet-O3 for 30 min. For the NIP device structure, the SnO2 electron transport layer (2.5%, diluted by water) was deposited on the ITO by spin-coating at 4000 rpm for 25 s, then annealed at 150 ℃ for 30 min in air. Before perovskite fabricating, the ITO/ SnO2 needs to UV-ozone treated for 15 min. Then put the substrate on the plat acceptor of the electrospray machine which was 60 mm below the nozzle, set the voltage to 20 KV and push speed to 0.001 mm/min.

The glass/ITO substrate was cleaned by ultrapure water and ethanol for 35 min and then blown dry with a a nitrogen gun and treated with ultraviolet-O3 for 30 min. For the NIP device structure, the SnO2 electron transport layer (2.5%, diluted by water) was deposited on the ITO by spin-coating at 4000 rpm for 25 s, then annealed at 150 ℃ for 30 min in air. The EQE curves were performed on the light source is a 300-W Xe lamp by an Enli Technology (Taiwan) EQE measurement system, which was calibrated by silicon diode with a known spectral response. The SPO stability tests were conducted in a nitrogen glove box by ageing devices under 1-sun illumination (white LED source, 100 mW/cm 2 ) with constant 0.9 V bias voltage at averaged temperature about 40 ℃ (temperature is kept in the range of 30-50 ℃). The open-circuit light stability tests were also conducted in a nitrogen glove box by ageing devices under 1-sun illumination (white LED source, 100 mW/cm 2 ). Notably, all devices are unencapsulated.

evidence.quote: Light stability of the perovskite films and devices. a,b) Normalized PL emission spectra of SP-based (a) and ES-based (b) perovskite films aged under illumination of white LED lamp (100 mW cm -2 ) for 0, 12, 48, and 87 h. c) Evolution of photovoltaic parameters in SP- and ES-based p-i-n devices at open-circuit condition under continuous illumination with a white LED lamp (100 mW cm -2 ) in a nitrogen atmosphere. d) Evolution of normalized PCE in SP- and ES-based p-i-n devices under SPO tracking under continuous illumination with a white LED lamp (100 mW cm -2 ) in a nitrogen atmosphere. e,f) Corresponding PL emission spectra of SP-based (e) and ES-based (f) perovskites before and after devices illumination. g,h) PL mapping spectra (with the emission peak position as the indicator) of SP-based (g) and ES-based (h) perovskite devices after illumination.

The operational stability of PSC devices was first evaluated by tracking the photovoltaic performance evolution under the open-circuit condition. ES-based p-i-n PSCs (with the device architecture of ITO/PTAA/Perovskite/C 60 /BCP/Au) retained 86% of their initial PCE (17.87% ± 0.48%) after 1056 h of illumination (white LED lamp, 100 mW cm -2 ). In contrast, SP-based devices only kept 65% of their original PCE (17.51% ± 0.87%) under the same conditions (Figure 3c). The PL spectra of corresponding devices are shown in Figure 3e,f, and a significant red shift ( ≈ 38 nm) was observed in SP samples alongside the broadened FWHM (from 53 to 89 nm in Table S6, Supporting Information) (Figure 3e).

evidence.quote: In addition, we performed the SPO tracking of unencapsulated devices under one-sun irradiation (white LED lamp, 100 mW cm -2 ) in N 2 . unresolved_notes: The Br-30 performance and stability passages establish p-i-n devices with x = 0.3 but do not identify the terminal metal used for those reported specimens. The fabrication procedure permits Au or Cu, so the Br-30 family retains this electrode identity as unresolved rather than guessing.

The fabrication procedure says the device was finished with Au or Cu, while the main-text p-i-n and n-i-p stability architectures explicitly use Au and a supporting comparison-table row reports a Cu p-i-n device. The Cu stack is therefore retained as a distinct family, but no supplied passage unambiguously links the reported champion/population/stability specimens to that Cu family.

Table S8 is described as covering forward and reverse scan directions, but its extracted rows provide only one SP row and one ES row without a direction column. Their J-V observations therefore have scan_direction not_reported.

The EQE caption reports separate integrated JSC values for SP- and ES-fabricated p-i-n PSC devices, but it does not establish that either was the same physical device as a best or champion J-V specimen. Separate EQE devices were retained.

The reported SP and ES ion-migration activation energies of 0.06 and 0.16 eV are group-level device-characterization results under dark conditions. The evidence does not identify individual devices or a population statistic, and the schema has no separate characterization-result entity, so they were not assigned to a champion specimen.

The alternative ES and SP fabrication recipes distinguish processing arms rather than device families. They are represented as explicitly alternative processing steps within the corresponding architecture families and as specimen/population variants.

The Br-15 specimens and the 5 × 5 cm 2 perovskite specimen are films used for materials characterization, not complete photovoltaic devices, and were excluded from device-family and performance records.

The supplied evidence reports thermal evaporation of “Au or Cu (100 nm)” but does not identify the terminal metal used for the Br-30 performance and stability specimens; the Br-30 family electrode identity therefore remains unresolved.

The activation energies of 0.06 and 0.16 eV are reported for SP- and ES-based device samples, respectively, but no supported individual-device identity is provided; they were not assigned to an IndividualDevice.

The two large-area tables report numerical J-V rows, but the supplied parser blocks do not independently identify the corresponding physical devices or unambiguously connect each table to the p-i-n versus n-i-p label; no large-area device or observation was added.

Table S8 describes forward and reverse scan directions, but its extracted table contains only one SP row and one ES row without a direction column. The Br-30 best-device observations therefore retain scan_direction as not_reported.
